data.narrative:
Neura Robotics is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $123.3M to date. The valuation analysis relies on a peer-median approach applied to a comparison set of 3 same-stage, same-sector companies: Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B). The broader comp universe includes 8 additional private robotics firms and 1 public comparable.

The stage-progression method was excluded due to data integrity concerns: applying a standard 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier to an inferred $1.4B base value would imply a $2.7B valuation, exceeding 20x the company's total capital raised and indicating an unreliable input source. The peer-median method is therefore the sole applicable triangulation approach. The three same-stage peers trade at a $1.6B–$2.0B range, with a median of $1.8B. This peer-median of $1.8B serves as the primary valuation point.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.5B–$2.0B, centered at $1.8B. This range reflects the variability across the peer set and applies a modest adjustment band around the median. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the three-company peer set for a Series B robotics company at Neura Robotics' specific stage of commercialization, and whether recent market conditions in frontier manufacturing technology have shifted relative valuations. The single applicable method limits triangulation robustness.
